subject: Onboarding benchmark readout + next steps for TerraHealth inference rollout
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soren Blake <soren@terrahealth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: TerraHealth inference onboarding — proposal for benchmark kickoff

Hi Soren,

Great kickoff yesterday — appreciate you and the team walking us through the expected production mix. To keep momentum, proposed next steps for the benchmarking window:

1) Benchmark window: Aug 10–12 (internal run Aug 6–8 to validate harness)
2) Targets we should validate during the acceptance run:
   - Throughput: sustained 250 concurrent req/s for typical 64-token prompts
   - Latency: p95 <= 300ms for text-generation short responses (<=256 tokens); p95 <= 450ms for longer 512-token summaries
   - Error budget: <=0.5% server errors over any 1-hr sliding window
3) Test hardware: initial run on dedi A100-80GB pool (matched to your SLA), fallback profile on g4dn-like instances for cost comparison
4) Artifacts I'll share today: a first-pass load plan + sample prompts (attached).

Can you confirm the target window works for your infra/compliance gate? If yes we'll split responsibilities and I'll loop Dev for the harness specifics.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: terrahealth-load-plan-v1.pdf (11 pages — test phases, measurement templates), sample_prompts_terrahealth.csv (100 sample prompts)

From: Soren Blake <soren@terrahealth.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: TerraHealth Onboarding Team <onboard@terrahealth.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TerraHealth inference onboarding — proposal for benchmark kickoff

Thanks Marcus — Aug 10–12 works for us. A couple quick constraints from infra and security:

- We need the run to use our staging dataset (PHI-masked) and an allowlist of IPs (will share CIDRs by Aug 4).
- Can we avoid the g4 fallback during acceptance? Our procurement needs the performance delta documented before we consider cheaper tiers.
- We'll want the final readout in a short PDF we can attach to our procurement packet.

I'll confirm the CIDRs and a point-of-contact for the staging data transfer by Aug 4.

—Soren
VP Product, TerraHealth

Looping Dev to confirm harness + metrics. Dev — can you confirm the following by EOD Aug 5 so we can lock the run?

- Exact load harness (k6 + goroutine-based client) and where the results will land (we prefer Drive + artifacts exported as CSV)
- Measurement breakdown: p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, token counts per request, and tail latencies per 1-minute window

Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TerraHealth inference onboarding — proposal for benchmark kickoff

Thanks — confirmed plan and short notes from the infra side:

- Harness: k6 driver with a lightweight Go runner and Redis-backed KV cache sim to approximate prefix caching. We'll push results to a Drive folder and attach CSVs.
- Test phases (brief):
   Phase A (smoke): 5–10 req/s ramp, verify correctness and auth
   Phase B (sustained): ramp to 250 req/s over 10m, hold 60m
   Phase C (stress): 350 req/s 5m bursts to observe error profile
- Measurement: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies at token checkpoints (64/256/512), GPU util, host CPU, network egress, and request-level error types
- Acceptance gates we'll enforce in the readout: p95 <=300ms (<=256 tokens), overall error-rate <=0.5%, and no sustained GPU OOMs.

I'll attach the exact k6 scenario in the Drive link and an example CSV schema.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Readout: TerraHealth Aug 10 acceptance run — results and recommended next steps

Hi Soren / TerraHealth team —

Thank you for a smooth acceptance window. Attached is a compact readout (readout-summary-20260819.pdf) and raw CSV exports in the Drive link. TL;DR: acceptance PASS with two recommended follow-ups.

Key results (sustained Phase B run, A100-80GB pool):
- Throughput: sustained 250 req/s for 60m with token mix matching your sample prompts (avg tokens/request ≈ 180)
- Latency: p95 = 285ms for <=256-token responses; p95 = 430ms for 512-token responses
- Error-rate: 0.32% total (transient 5xx spikes observed during Phase C stress bursts only)
- Observations: KV cache hit-rate averaged 68% after warmup; GPU util averaged 76% during sustained run

Acceptance gates: all met (p95 thresholds, error budget).

Recommended next steps:
1) Canary rollout: provision a small Dedicated pool (2x A100) and run a 48-hour production traffic mirror for further verification (we'll help automate rollback triggers).
2) Cost/comparison: separate follow-up to model projected unit cost if you choose a g4-type fallback; we will not enable the fallback automatically during your procurement review per your ask.
3) Docs: we'll produce a one-page executive summary for procurement and upload the full readout + CSVs to the Drive link.

Action items and owners:
- Redwood: finalize readout PDF and upload raw CSVs (Marcus, Dev) — by EOD Aug 19 (done, attached).
- TerraHealth: confirm canary window and preferred start date for Dedicated pool — Soren (target week of Aug 23).
- Lauren (Redwood): finalize allowlist and transfer credentials with TerraHealth POC (onboarding@terrahealth.ai).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min readout next week to walk the exec summary with procurement.

Thanks again — delighted to get you across the acceptance threshold.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: readout-summary-20260819.pdf
Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/terrahealth/ONBOARD-TH-0442
